checks.question: Is the phased-motion reordering in _draw_ships correct and free of GL-state leakage between the trail, hull and glow phases?
checks.evidence: render/renderer.py:1430-1448. Trail phase is a self-contained helper (1453-1478: enables blend, sets SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, depth mask false, push/translate/rotate/begin/end/pop, depth mask true, blend disabled). Hull phase reuses the unchanged _draw_ship, which is matrix-balanced (glPushMatrix 2068 / glPopMatrix 2143) and restores texture+lighting (2141-2142). Glow phase (1446-1448) uses _draw_ship_glow (1480-1497), which restores depth mask and blend and defers blend-func reset to _draw_glow (1007). Independent in-memory command-stream oracle (compiled HEAD and worktree draw methods, recorded glEnable/glDisable/glDepthMask/glBlendFunc/glPushMatrix/glPopMatrix/glCallList): net GL state at end of the pass is identical to HEAD in all 8 scenes (blend enabled/disabled, depth mask, matrix depth 0, final material), e.g. mixed authored+legacy moving head={'blend': False,'depth_mask': True,'pushpop': 0,'mat': ('matte',)} new=identical. Trail/glow vertex data, colour and radius are line-for-line the same as the gated blocks they replace (2075-2091 vs 1453-1478; 2145-2158 vs 1480-1497).
checks.notes: One real semantic consequence of hoisting trails: trails are alpha-blended with depth writes off, so a trail drawn before another ship's hull is overpainted by that (even farther) hull, and the trail also inherits a different leftover texture coordinate (GL_TEXTURE_2D + GL_MODULATE is bound with no glTexCoord2f) and a different fixed-function specular state than in the old per-entity order. This ordering already exists in the cached production path (1383-1397), so the change makes the uncached path match it rather than introducing a new production artifact; see finding F1.

checks.question: Do legacy-only scenes and mixed legacy/authored fleets take exactly the previous per-entity path (no new material calls, no suppression change, no reordering)?
checks.evidence: Legacy-only: PASS. Command-stream diff of the pre-delta code (git show HEAD:render/renderer.py) against the working tree, both compiled from real AST bodies: 'legacy-only moving x2' 91 events identical, 'legacy-only motionless' 59 identical, 'legacy station alone' 35 identical, 'legacy ships + station' 80 identical (uncached), and 157/117/67/138 identical (cached). No material calls, suppression or ordering change on those paths, and the added predicate only calls _ship_size() earlier (renderer-local memo, no GL effect). Mixed: FAIL AS STATED. 'mixed authored+legacy moving' head=91 vs new=100 events: both ships' trails are hoisted ahead of all hulls and both glows deferred; the legacy hull's trail is now emitted before the authored hull. 'mixed authored moveless + legacy moving' shows the scene-wide predicate moving a legacy ship's trail even though the authored ship is stationary (head=75 vs new=80). The reordering is deliberate and documented in the new comment (1426-1429), and legacy hull/role/material submission itself is unchanged.
checks.notes: This branch is not reachable from the production draw loop: render/renderer.py:495 is the only call site and always passes a frame cache from _ensure_frame_cache, which never returns None, so mixed-scene reordering affects only harnesses that call _draw_ships(selection, None) (native-parity.py 'uncached' mode, parity-state-probe.py, tests). If 'byte-identical mixed fleets' is a hard requirement, the predicate would have to be per-entity, which defeats the stated goal of matching the cached ordering.

checks.question: Is the authored-only LOD suppression change in _draw_ship_role_batch correct, and is legacy suppression unchanged?
checks.evidence: render/renderer.py:1529-1534: `authored = is_authored(size.shape) if ':' in size.shape else False`, then both cuts are guarded by `not authored`, so for authored=False the predicates are textually identical to HEAD. Legacy retention is measured, not assumed: tests/test_s07_authored_lod_parity.py:60-77 drives the real role batch for 'rebel:battleship', 'unregistered:custom' (colon, not authored) and 'needle' at 0/1/16±eps/34±eps/60 px and asserts base-only <16, base+lit <34, all roles >=34. Authored non-suppression is measured at apparent=8 px: tests/test_s07_motion_order.py:79-86 asserts 6 glCallList for the authored ship and 1 for the legacy ship (hulls=7 cached / 12 uncached). tests/test_s07_authored_lod_parity.py:14-35 mutates the compiled AST to restore the old unconditional suppression and asserts the old behaviour is detected (changed==2 guards), which is a live negative control that the change is load-bearing.
checks.notes: Authored hulls now lose the LOD optimisation entirely, down to apparent 0 px (see finding F2: 5 extra display-list submissions plus shader uniform updates per authored ship per frame at zoom-out).

checks.question: Can the draw_motion gate in _draw_ship suppress motion for legacy callers (default value), and does the authored accent material call leak to legacy?
checks.evidence: Signature is `def _draw_ship(self, e: Entity, draw_motion=True)` (2057); the only call passing False is the phased branch (1441). The other caller, tests/test_ship_sizes.py:61/73, calls r._draw_ship(e) positionally, so it keeps both trail (2080) and glow (2145). Accent material: the new `if authored: self._material_matte()` (2124-2126) is guarded, and tests/test_s07_material_parity.py:75-80 pins the legacy uncached accent at {'shininess': 12.0, 'spec': (0.85,0.85,0.85)} - the trim metal value that HEAD also leaves in place - so an unguarded matte would turn the test red. My command-stream diff of an authored ship shows exactly one added ('matte',) event and of a legacy ship shows none.
checks.notes: Gate thresholds are identical to the helpers: trail spd>2 (2080 vs 1456), glow spd>8 (2145 vs 1483), same segment_visible/_in_front/is_position_visible calls. _draw_ship still computes spd/trail_length/tail when draw_motion is False (dead arithmetic, no GL).

checks.question: Do the _draw_station authored material additions leave the legacy alloy path untouched?
checks.evidence: render/renderer.py:2544-2547 adds per-role _material_metal only under `if authored_station`, and 2556-2557 adds a guarded matte before the accent. Command-stream diff (real _draw_station AST, HEAD vs worktree): 'legacy station uncached' 35 events identical, including metal(8.0,(0.5,0.55,0.62)) before base/dark/trim and no matte before the accent. 'authored station uncached' adds exactly four events and nothing else: metal(8.0,(0.42,0.42,0.42)) before base, metal(8.0,(0.42,0.42,0.42)) before dark, metal(12.0,(0.85,0.85,0.85)) before trim, matte before accent. Cached authored station is unchanged (67 events identical pre/post). tests/test_s07_material_parity.py:55-63 asserts cached vs uncached per-glCallList state (key + material + lighting + texture + shader uniforms) is equal for both shader-available and fixed-function fallback, and 64-72 pins the legacy accent at the alloy 8.0/(0.50,0.55,0.62) value.
checks.notes: Two honest qualifications. (a) The authored path still emits the pre-existing alloy metal(8.0,(0.50,0.55,0.62)) at 2537, immediately overwritten by the first per-role call with no draw in between - harmless but redundant, so authored stations issue 5 material calls and legacy 2. (b) With the hull program bound, glMaterial is inert: HULL in render/fleet_materials.py computes its own specular (`spec`, `polish`) from uniforms and never reads gl_FrontMaterial, so only the accent matte (drawn outside `materials.use`, 2556-2560) is visually effective; the parity achieved for base/dark/trim is command-level, not appearance-level.

checks.question: Are the tests honest oracles that trace real production AST or drive real code rather than restating the implementation?
checks.evidence: test_s07_motion_order.py:15-70 does ast.parse(render/renderer.py), compiles the real _draw_ships/_draw_ship/_draw_ship_trail/_draw_ship_glow bodies, and asserts `ns[name].__globals__ is ns` plus `__globals__['glCallList'] is ns['glCallList']` (67-69) so recorders are not shadowed by stale copies; assertions are on observed call order/counts, not on source text. test_s07_material_parity.py:9-59 drives the real _draw_ships/_draw_station bodies and records the GL state at each glCallList (key, material, shader uniforms, lighting, texture); its two legacy tests would fail on exactly the two plausible mistakes (unguarded matte in _draw_ship, unguarded metal in _draw_station). test_s07_capture_transition.py:41-105 drives real Renderer/Camera/InputController, patches every gl* in render.renderer and render.camera to raise (fail closed, 125-135), builds expected bounds independently from the manifest raw mesh and frame_oracle, and asserts camera._camera_boxes contains them plus state_hash unchanged. test_s07_authored_lod_parity.py:14-35 is an in-memory AST mutation control.
checks.notes: Gaps, not dishonesty. (i) test_s07_motion_order.py:75-78 uses shape 'needle' (no colon) for its legacy control, so deleting the `is_authored(...)` clause from phased_motion (leaving `':' in self._ship_size(e).shape`) would leave all four motion-order tests green - the colon-but-unregistered case is untested for the motion predicate (finding F5). (ii) test_s07_capture_transition.py never calls the four changed methods; it exercises _ship_size/_visual_hit/picking, so it is honest but orthogonal to this delta. (iii) test_s07_material_parity.py records no matrix, blend or depth state, so it cannot detect that class of leak (my C1 evidence comes from an independent oracle, not from it).

checks.evidence: Read of 1419-1448, 1499-1534, 2057-2158 and 2519-2583: every entity attribute is read (e.alive, e.is_planet, e.is_station, e.pos, e.yaw, e.vel.length(), e.owner, e.data_id, e.radius, e.build_queue / build_queue[0].get); no assignment targets e.*, state.*, tick, queue or selection. The only writes reachable are renderer-local: _ship_size memoises scope['sizes'] (1974-1985), _px_per_world memoises scope['projection'] (3715-3717), and the ship/station display-list caches (ship_lists) - all pre-existing and render-only. test_s07_capture_transition.py asserts state_hash(state) == before and selection._generation unchanged across the consumers it exercises (94-99).

findings.detail: In a mixed legacy/authored fleet with any ship moving faster than 2 units/s, the scene-wide predicate reorders legacy hulls too: all trails are hoisted ahead of all hulls and all glows deferred. This is documented intent, but it means mixed scenes are not command-identical to the pre-delta uncached path, contrary to a literal 'byte-identical mixed fleet' requirement. Beyond ordering, a hoisted trail is alpha-blended with depth writes off and inherits a different leftover texture coordinate (GL_TEXTURE_2D + GL_MODULATE is bound and the trail sets no glTexCoord) and a different fixed-function specular state, so trail colour can shift slightly in overlap cases. Production never reaches this branch (only call site 495 always passes a cache), and the cached path already had this ordering; no test measures either effect.

Authored hulls now submit all six roles at every apparent size, including sub-pixel. The LOD cut exists to avoid per-entity GL work at zoom-out, so every authored ship now costs 5 extra display-list calls plus push/pop, colour and two shader uniform updates per frame regardless of how small it is. Intended for parity with the uncached path, but there is no absolute floor (e.g. apparent < 1 px) and no performance evidence in the delta.

The authored station path keeps the pre-existing alloy _material_metal(8.0, (0.50,0.55,0.62)) at 2537 and immediately overwrites it with metal(8.0,(0.42,...)) before the base draw, so it issues 5 material calls where legacy issues 2, with one entirely redundant. More importantly, while the hull program is bound (the production case) all four role-material calls are inert because HULL computes specular from `materialPass`/`authoredSurface` and never reads gl_FrontMaterial; only the accent matte is visually effective. The 'matches the cached role materials' claim is therefore command-level, not appearance-level, and the native parity harness cannot distinguish the two.

Trail and glow logic is now duplicated: _draw_ship keeps inline copies (2075-2091, 2145-2158) of _draw_ship_trail (1453-1478) and _draw_ship_glow (1480-1497). They agree today (verified line by line: same trail_length, tail, colour, alpha, three vertices; same glow radius/colour), but nothing in the CPU suite compares them - test_s07_material_parity noops trail/glow and test_s07_motion_order records only event kind. Having _draw_ship delegate to the helpers (or having the helpers call back) would make drift impossible.

The legacy control sets selected=False so _ship_size returns 'needle' (no colon). Mutating phased_motion to `':' in self._ship_size(e).shape` (dropping the is_authored clause) would still yield False for that control and True for the authored cases, so all four tests stay green while a namespaced-but-unregistered hull (e.g. 'unregistered:custom') would silently trigger phased motion in legacy scenes. A control with a colon-bearing, non-authored shape would close this.

The parity oracle compares the state recorded at each glCallList, which cannot see matrix-stack, blend or depth-mask leaks, and it only compares cached vs uncached for authored rows. The pre-existing legacy divergence is preserved and pinned rather than closed: cached legacy accent is drawn with matte (0.0/0,0,0) while uncached legacy accent is drawn with 12.0/(0.85,0.85,0.85) for ships and 8.0/(0.50,0.55,0.62) for stations. A reader should not conclude from these tests that the uncached capture path is appearance-faithful for legacy rows.

The scaffold exclusion is not a blank cheque: the row's own appearance decision is asserted (exactly one, approval_kind 'appearance-scaffold-revision', assets == ['shared:construction_scaffold'], owner words), its execution authority is asserted (exactly one, 'authorized-execution-not-appearance'), the exclusion is by literal identity (`separate = {SCAFFOLD}`) and is bounded by `len(pipeline['assets']) == 103`, `core - separate == expected` and `set(entries) - separate == expected`, and every other non-S06 row is still asserted unregistered with an allowed legacy status. assert_preview_boundary also proves mesh_for(SCAFFOLD) is None with preview OFF (start and after configure({})) and non-None only with preview ON. Residual gaps: the guard never asserts rows[SCAFFOLD]['envelope_decision'] == its appearance decision (the registry does carry that value), and its hash loop is restricted to S06 `requested`, so approved-s07-scaffold-source-hashes.json is verified elsewhere (tests/test_s07_scaffold_registration.py), not here. Both registered controls (test_s06_appearance_records.py:209 and :215) still raise AssertionError and are sensitive: neither removed decision is referenced by any other guard assertion.

`previous_approvals_sha256` (7866c814) describes an uncommitted intermediate approvals.json and cannot be recomputed from any committed state, so it is plausible but unverifiable. `approved_revisions_preserved` mixes two meanings: entries with historical_pin_matches_current false (tools/art/alliance_common.py, twice) are preserved against the published checkpoint, not against the B5 approval pin. The field names state this and no claim is overstated, but a reader scanning only `preserved_against_published_checkpoint: true` could infer the approved bytes are unchanged.

independent_reproduction.result: 19 tests OK (exit 0) and 11 registration-guard controls OK (exit 0). AST diff: exactly the four named methods changed; protected methods AST-equal; B5 runtime pin equals the measured 9aff3414. Command-stream oracle: legacy-only scenes byte-identical pre/post (uncached 91/59/35/80 events, cached 157/117/67/138); mixed moving scenes differ only by motion phasing plus the authored matte; net GL state at end of pass identical to HEAD in all 8 scenes with matrix depth 0; authored station adds exactly 3 metal calls and 1 matte and legacy station adds none.

limitations: The camera exposes no native snapshot-generation field (render/camera.py contains no 'snapshot' or '_generation' at all), so tests/test_s07_capture_transition.py reports the selection generation captured before camera.refresh_scene() as `snapshot_generation`. It is the selection generation at explicit refresh, not a native snapshot counter; the measurement cannot prove the camera froze the same snapshot the renderer consumed.

No native GL or pixel execution was performed by this review (prohibited, and a concurrent native capture process shares the machine). native-motion-transition-attempt3/report.json claims status passed, renderer_sha256 9aff3414 and exact cached/uncached parity on 6 rows, but it is implementer-produced, I did not reproduce it, every captured subject is asserted to resolve in the registry (so no legacy-only and no mixed legacy/authored scene is covered), and it compares the two post-change paths with each other rather than against the pre-change uncached appearance.

The command-stream oracle compiles only the six draw functions and fakes the materials/shader, display-list, glow and material helpers; it proves call order and fixed-function state, not rasterised pixels or shader output.
tests/test_s07_scaffold_registration.py was read but not run, so the scaffold-only provenance/hash coverage it delegates to is unverified here.
`previous_approvals_sha256` in parity-pin-reconciliation-v2.json refers to an uncommitted intermediate file and is unverifiable.

Only the four changed methods, their immediate helpers, the named tests and the B5 pin record were audited; the wider S06/S07 approval corpus, the capture harnesses themselves and the rest of renderer.py were not re-reviewed.
Performance claims (LOD cost of always-on authored roles) are reasoned from the code, not measured.
